chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Allah informed us through Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashm, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was taken on the Night Journey and prayer time arrived, Jibril (peace be upon him) gave the call to prayer. Whenever he said: 'Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest,' the angels said: 'Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest.' When he said: 'I bear witness that there is no god but Allah,' the angels said: 'He has cast off the idols.' When he said: 'I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah,' the angels said: 'A prophet has been sent.' When he said: 'Come to prayer,' the angels said: 'He urges [us] to worship his Lord.' When he said: 'Come to success,' the angels said: 'He who follows him will succeed.'
ai.seo_question: What did the angels say in response to each part of the Prophet's call to prayer during the Night Journey?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, this narration elucidates the metaphysical dimensions of the Adhan by linking each phrase to a specific angelic response, thereby validating the call as a divine decree rather than a mere human announcement. It underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the spiritual efficacy of the Adhan, where the angels' declarations confirm the theological truths of Tawhid, Nabuwwah, and the invitation to salvation.
